surprises.description: CLW guided to only $10–20 million of Q4 adjusted EBITDA, well below the preview’s $35–40 million threshold for validating the recovery. The company cited seasonal volume declines, Augusta disruptions, Cypress Bend maintenance, and higher seasonal energy costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company guided Q4 2026 adjusted EBITDA to $10-20 million,” reflecting “seasonal volume declines, continued Augusta disruptions, $5-7 million in Cypress Bend maintenance costs, and ~$4 million in seasonal energy cost increases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q4 guide ≥ $35–40M EBITDA — required to validate a ~$140M 2027 run-rate.”

surprises.description: The preview described the two $60-per-ton increases as worth $50–60 million annually, but the call said the first $60-per-ton increase is fully implemented and is expected to deliver more than $70 million annually. That is a stronger stated benefit, although the facts do not give the implementation status of the second increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The first $60/ton price increase is fully implemented and expected to deliver more than $70 million in annual benefit.”

surprises.description: The preview expected Q3 net sales of $388.4 million, while CLW reported $385 million, a small miss; sales were down 4% year over year versus the preview’s 2.7% expected decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net sales fell 4% year-over-year to $385 million, driven by lower market-based pricing and a 1% decline in shipments.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed serious Augusta mill operating failures and a larger, longer-lasting maintenance burden than the preview identified: the mill had been running below needed production, unplanned capital investment was required, and two outages are now expected in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operational failures in the pulp, power and recovery areas of the Augusta mill caused it to run roughly 10-15% below needed production over recent quarters, requiring additional unplanned capital investment.” Maintenance was “deferred to January 2027 at an estimated $12-15 million,” with another outage in Q2 or Q3 2027 “costing $7-10 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that CLW was “struggling to deliver products on time,” but did not describe Augusta production failures or these 2027 outage costs.

surprises.description: CLW reported substantial Middle East conflict-related costs that the preview did not identify: about $12 million in Q3, nearly $30 million for the year, and another $1–2 million expected in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Middle East conflict-related costs totaled approximately $12 million in Q3 and are approaching $30 million for the full year, with an additional $1-2 million expected in Q4.”

surprises.description: CLW received a further $17.5 million insurance payment in Q3, identified as the final payment. The preview cited $33 million of recoveries through Q2 and expected $33 million of insurance recoveries to aid FY26 cash flow, so this additional payment was not reflected in that stated expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company received a fourth and final representation and warranty insurance payment of $17.5 million,” bringing total recoveries to $73 million; “$9.5 million of Q3 recoveries offset Augusta operational losses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guide: positive FCF, capex $65–75M, $20–30M working-capital release, aided by $33M insurance recoveries and ~$30M tax refunds.”

surprises.description: The call announced that CFO Sherri Baker will leave in a few weeks for a new opportunity in Texas; the preview did not flag an impending CFO departure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Sherri Baker is leaving the company in a few weeks for a new opportunity in Texas after more than three years in the role.”
